Article Title: Channi vs Warring: Why Sachin Pilot may be Congress's best bet in Punjab
Article Text:
Congress has handed Sachin Pilot a familiar problem and a bigger opportunity.

Why Congress was forced to budge

Bhupesh Baghel had asserted that it is not a 'child's play' and the decision of the high command will not change.

Why Sachin Pilot

Punjab Congress working president welcomed Sachin Pilot’s appointment, saying it will help iron out differences within the state unit.

Baghel gone. Will Warring be next?

Congress has a lot at stake

Punjab could shape Pilot's Rajasthan future

NEW DELHI: The Congress leadership last week finally responded to 'Mayday' calls from Punjab rebels and brought in Sachin Pilot , replacing Bhupesh Baghel , to prevent a crash landing of the deeply fractured state unit ahead of the assembly elections early next year.Months of open infighting between Charanjit Singh Channi, the former chief minister leading the rebel camp, and Raja Warring, the state unit chief, not just embarrassed the Congress but also threatened to derail its 2027 campaign.Before being put in the driver's seat in Punjab, Pilot was in charge of Chhattisgarh, where Baghel remains a key Congress leader and former chief minister.The Congress had sent former Chhattisgarh chief minister Bhagel to Punjab in February this year to defuse the brewing Channi vs Warring crisis in the state unit. Ironically, as things turned out, Baghel faced resistance and became part of the crisis, with the Channi camp openly accusing him of siding with Warring. More so, since July, after the party’s central leadership decided to ignore Channi’s claim for the top post in the state and announced that it would continue with Warring as state Congress president.With several senior state leaders backing Channi, the fight turned ugly and Baghel became ineffective.Congress meetings in the districts saw open “Go back Baghel” chants from Channi supporters, taking the infighting to the streets and embarrassing the top leadership.So, while the ruling Aam Aadmi Party was already in full election mode with chief minister Bhagwant Mann at the centre of its campaign, the Congress was still struggling to get its senior leadership to sit across the table.Not just the AAP, even the BJP and the Akalis had their house in order and were planning their electoral moves on the ground. With the party's 2027 campaign failing to take off under Baghel, the Congress was forced to budge and turn to Pilot.The Congress decision to send Pilot to Punjab, while ironic, may still be the best bet for the leadership. Sachin Pilot, during his years in the Congress, has seen enough internal wars to know how quickly a fight over one post can turn into a larger battle over leadership, political space and, of course, eventually the chief minister's chair.Throwback to Rajasthan, where he spent years at the centre of a similar leadership tussle with senior leader Ashok Gehlot. Pilot brings something the Congress needs badly right now: the experience of being at the centre of a difficult internal power struggle.Pilot has led the Rajasthan unit, worked closely with the high command, weathered the bitter internal battle, survived the fallout and then rebuilt his position within the Congress.He was appointed Rajasthan Congress chief in 2014, after the party's abysmal performance in the 2013 assembly election. Over the next four years, he emerged as one of the key faces of the party's rebuilding effort before Congress returned to power in 2018. That victory, however, did not give him the chief minister's chair.Ashok Gehlot became chief minister, while Pilot was made deputy chief minister and continued as PCC president. While both sides got something, the arrangement never really settled the rivalry between Gehlot and Pilot.By 2020, those differences exploded into an open rebellion.Pilot left Jaipur with a group of MLAs and challenged the Gehlot government. Congress responded by removing him as deputy chief minister and state president. The Gehlot camp even accused him of working with the BJP. A truce was eventually worked out, and Pilot stayed with Congress.But he never quite returned to the position he had occupied before and has been on the sidelines ever since. He remained a prominent face in the party and was later given charge of Chhattisgarh, but his role in Rajasthan remained limited.It is interesting how, in Rajasthan, Pilot was the leader asking the Congress high command to listen to a dissatisfied camp. In Punjab, he now has to convince dissatisfied leaders to accept the high command's decisions and work together.That may be why Congress believes he is best suited for the job.But will Pilot’s appointment end the crisis in the Punjab unit?Channi's supporters had demanded Warring be removed as Punjab Congress chief, and the Jalandhar MP be declared Congress’s chief ministerial face for the 2027 assembly polls. The Congress has not accepted either of the two demands. So, while Channi has not made any significant gains, Warring has been left wondering if he will be the next to be axed.Warring was picked up to lead and rebuild the Punjab unit after the Congress was decimated in the 2022 assembly polls. Channi, who was the chief minister then, led the Congress to its worst-ever performance in the state. The Congress not just lost its government to AAP but was also reduced to 18 seats in the 117-member assembly.The leadership tussle between the two had been brewing for quite some time. But as is the Congress’s wont, the party kept dilly-dallying on the issue for nearly 4 years. Finally, when the Congress did take a decision, it ended up opening deep faultlines.For now, both camps have welcomed his appointment. Warring said Pilot's energy and dynamism would "for sure" add to the vigour of the party ahead of the crucial polls, while Gurdaspur MP Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa, a close associate of Channi, said Pilot's experience, leadership and connect with the people would give new strength and momentum to the Congress in Punjab.Punjab Congress working president Raj Kumar Verka hopes that under Pilot’s leadership all state leaders would come together. "Pilot knows all leaders of Punjab, and they also have confidence in him," said Verka.For Pilot, this may be his first real test. If party leadership decides to keep Warring, he has to get Channi, Randhawa and other leaders to fall in line. If Warring goes, he has to make sure one problem is not replaced by the other.The Congress, which remains the main challenger for now, cannot afford this infighting because Punjab is one of the states where it still has a real chance. There is anti-incumbency against the Bhagwant Mann-led AAP government.In 2022, AAP swept 92 of the 117 assembly seats, while Congress was reduced to 18. But the 2024 Lok Sabha election brought some relief for the grand old party. The Congress won seven of Punjab's 13 seats, compared with AAP's three, showing that the party still has enough ground to be a serious challenger.AAP is perhaps no longer riding the wave that brought it to power in 2022 and is now defending its record under Bhagwant Mann. Raghav Chadha's exit has also added to the churn in the party.The BJP and the Akalis are still on the margins of the state’s politics. But the scenario could change very fast. The BJP is going all out to broaden its organisational base and rope in leaders from other parties. There are also reports of talks between the BJP and the Akalis to revive their old alliance. The Congress needs to remember that the BJP is coming off a massive victory in West Bengal and is looking to expand its footprint in Punjab as well.Pilot has already made it clear that he sees Punjab as a comeback opportunity for the Congress. On Monday, he said he was confident that with a strong organisation, collective effort and the energy of party workers, Congress could return to power in the state.Pilot has the experience of being a part of successful strategising in Himachal Pradesh in the previous assembly polls and has also been a senior observer for the Kerala polls, where Congress returned to power after a decade.If Pilot can manage to bring the rival Punjab camps together and help the Congress put up a strong show in 2027, it will add to his standing within the party at a time when Rajasthan is already looking ahead to the 2028 assembly election.There has long been speculation over a bigger role for Pilot in Rajasthan. He may not have got it yet, but a successful Punjab stint could considerably strengthen his case.For a leader who has had to rebuild his own position in the party before, Punjab could well become the next big step in that comeback.
Article Summary: Congress has handed Sachin Pilot a familiar problem and a bigger opportunity. Pilot has seen enough internal wars to know how quickly a fight over one post can turn into a larger battle over leadership, political space and, of course, eventually the chief minister's chair.

Article Title: Artist puts Kashmiri poet Lal Ded's mysticism on Pashmina
Article Text:
Lal Ded, also known as Lalleshwari, was born near Srinagar in a Kashmiri Pandit family

Lal Ded walked barefoot, wandered, spoke in riddles.

SRINAGAR: MF Husain’s horses meant power. Flat, bold, Cubist, built for scale like the Bollywood billboards he once painted in Mumbai. Masood Hussain’s horse is painted on Pashmina and dyed in the wool — carrying the earliest Kashmiri poetry, passed down orally for 600 years before anyone wrote it down.This is a sharp turn from familiar ground for Srinagar-based Hussain, whose work for years has chronicled Kashmir’s conflict, grief and everyday life. For the first time, he has painted Lal Vakhs — mystical four-line verses of 14th-century Kashmiri poet Lal Ded — on Pashmina shawls.Twenty shawls. Two years. “These are painted shawls based on Lal Vakhs. I selected 20 Vakhs, then I conceived them and painted them,” Hussain said Monday at an exhibition in Srinagar.Lal Ded, also known as Lalleshwari, was born near Srinagar in a Kashmiri Pandit family. Abused at her marital home, she left at 26 to become an itinerant Shaiva mystic. Muslims called her Lal Arifa. Her Vakhs — from the Sanskrit vaak, meaning “speech” or “saying” — are among the earliest compositions in Kashmiri and a foundation of its literary tradition.Hussain’s shawls give those words a visual life. One features what Hussain calls a celestial horse — a rider moving beneath a sky stitched with constellations.Other shawls turn towards Lal Ded’s references to death, spiritual passage and the unseen.The idea took root after Hussain’s collaborations with Irish poet Gabriel Rosenstock, who died of cancer in April this year. Their first project marked Mahatma Gandhi’s 150th birth anniversary. Rosenstock’s 150 minimalist haikus and tankas were paired with Hussain’s watercolours, bringing Irish culture, Kashmiri artistry and Gandhian philosophy of peace into one book.“I mostly painted Kashmir and its conflict. Once I collaborated with Rosenstock, a lot changed,” Hussain said. “Why not work on Kashmir Sufism, Rishi culture, syncretic culture and convert them into paintings? Why not start on Lal Ded on Pashmina? I got the idea.”Lal Ded walked barefoot, wandered, spoke in riddles. Hussain began by reading extensively about her and her poetry. “A lot has been written, but no one has given it a visual shape. I tried,” Hussain said. The medium is the message. It is an old poetry in a new skin — mysticism that can be worn.
Article Summary: Masood Hussain’s horse is painted on Pashmina and dyed in the wool. It carries the earliest Kashmiri poetry, passed down orally for 600 years. Lal Vakhs are mystical four-line verses of 14th-century Kashmiri poet Lal Ded. Hussain began by reading extensively about her and her poetry.

Article Title: "I felt let down as a wife and as a mother": Has Gisele Bündchen spoken about why she ended her marriage to Tom Brady?

Tom Brady, the seven time Super Bowl champion, was married to Brazilian supermodel Gisele Bündchen for thirteen years before they ended their marriage in 2022. While it has been a couple of years since their separation, neither Tom Brady nor Gisele Bündchen has spoken about the reason behind it.No, the former Victoria’s Secret model Gisele Bündchen has made no such claims about her marriage to the New England Patriots’ legend Tom Brady.A fanpage on X made a fake post that read as, “Gisele Bündchen reportedly opened up about the reasons behind the end of her marriage to Tom Brady, making several explosive claims about their relationship and family life. According to the statement, Gisele felt that Tom was often absent and failed to give their family the attention she believed they deserved.”The post added, “”I felt let down as a wife and as a mother watching everything unfold.” She also addressed accusations of infidelity and the difficult moments in their relationship, saying that resentment and regret eventually consumed their marriage. According to the claims, Gisele eventually gave Tom an ultimatum, asking him to prioritize either his family or his football career. “He made it clear that he had built his career long before I came into his life and that he wasn’t prepared to walk away from it, even for his family.That was when I realized I had to make a decision for myself.””The post is entirely fake as Gisele Bündchen has made no such claims about her divorce to Tom Brady.Months after their divorce, Gisele Bündchen sat for an interview with Vogue where she said the reason behind their divorce is not so “black and white”.Despite the post on X being fake, it has sparked a heated debate among fans.A fan took to X and wrote, “She finally said what a lot of people already knew. He built his whole identity around football, she built hers around the family they actually had, and when she asked him to choose, he chose the game.”Another fan posted, “That sounds like years of hurt and resentment building up. 💔 No matter how successful someone is, being present for your family matters too. Sometimes love alone isn’t enough when two people want different things from life.A third fan posted, “She’s called the ultimatum story hurtful rumor, said the split was more complicated than football vs. family, and that she has no regrets and still wants Tom to be happy.”Another fan noted, “This is recycled fake news. Gisele has already addressed these exact claims years ago and denied giving any ultimatum. She described the split as them growing apart, not this dramatic version. Same fabricated quotes keep getting reposted for engagement.”
Article Summary: A fanpage on X made a fake post that read as, “Gisele Bündchen reportedly opened up about the reasons behind the end of her marriage to Tom Brady, making several explosive claims about their relationship and family life” According to the claims, Gisele eventually gave Tom an ultimatum, asking him to prioritize either his family or his football career. The post has sparked a heated debate among fans.

Article Title: 'Suffered from hypertension, diabetes': Ex-Delhi chief secretary dies by suicide; note says no one responsible
Article Text:
Former Delhi chief secretary Rakesh Mehta was found dead in his Noida flat.





NOIDA: Former Delhi chief secretary and municipal commissioner Rakesh Mehta , 74, was found dead at his rented flat in Sector 82 on Sunday afternoon.Police recovered a one-page note in which the retired bureaucrat referred to his illnesses and stated that no one was responsible for his death.Mehta had been living alone at Central Vihar-2 for around five years. His wife, also a retired Delhi-cadre IAS officer, and their son live in Dehradun, while their married daughter is based in London. Family members visited him in Noida from time to time.According to police, Mehta's wife last spoke to him on Saturday night. When repeated calls went unanswered on Sunday afternoon, family members alerted the society's security staff. Two guards went to his flat and found him dead in one of the rooms. A police team and a relative living nearby arrived soon afterwards.A forensic team examined the flat and collected evidence before the body was sent for an autopsy. Till late Tuesday night, the family had not lodged any complaint, though police said an inquiry had been initiated into the circumstances surrounding the death.Family members said Mehta had been suffering from hypertension, diabetes and other health problems, including tremors in his right hand and leg.A 1975-batch AGMUT-cadre IAS officer, Mehta took charge as Delhi chief secretary in December 2007 during the Sheila Dikshit government's tenure and remained in the post until 2010. His tenure included preparations for the 2010 Commonwealth Games, one of the biggest administrative challenges faced by the capital.Before becoming chief secretary, Mehta served in several key positions, including as MCD commissioner, chairman and managing director of Delhi Transport Corporation, and secretary (power). He was known for his focus on urban governance and public transport.During his stint at DTC, Mehta oversaw the transition away from the accident-prone Blue Line buses and the introduction of low-floor buses, which went on to become a familiar feature of Delhi's roads.Known as a media-savvy bureaucrat who pushed new projects and reforms, Mehta unveiled a 10-point agenda after taking charge as chief secretary. He also advocated greater transparency in civic administration, including changes to building bylaws, and promoted the use of technology to bring government services closer to citizens.Mehta studied at St Stephen's College, JNU and the London School of Economics. His final rites were held in Delhi on Monday.
Article Summary: Rakesh Mehta, 74, was found dead at his rented flat in Sector 82 on Sunday. Police recovered a one-page note in which the retired bureaucrat referred to his illnesses and stated that no one was responsible for his death. Family members visited him in Noida from time to time.

NEW DELHI: Japan will face India in a historic men's T20I on September 22 at the Sano International Cricket Ground. India are the ICC Men's T20 World Cup champions and the No. 1 ranked side. Japan have already announced the squad that will take on India.The match will be Japan's first step in their preparation for the Asian Games in Nagoya, which begin two days later.Japan's all-time leading T20I run-scorer Kendel Kadowaki-Fleming will lead the team. Ibrahim Takahashi and Declan Suzuki-McComb are the other two players in the squad who have played more than 50 T20Is.The squad is the same group that Japan have picked for their Asian Games campaign.Japan have left out players who are eligible to play T20Is under ICC rules but cannot play at the Asian Games under its rules.This has opened the door for emerging spin-bowling all-rounder Jake Kusuda-Nairn, who impressed in domestic cricket.Spinner Tsuyoshi Takada also returns to the squad. He first played for Japan at the ICC East Asia-Pacific Twenty20 Championship in 2013.The squad includes Wataru Miyauchi and Makoto Taniyama, who studied at Japanese schools with cricket Bukatsu programs.Taniyama is a leg-spinner who developed his bowling action by watching Shane Warne videos on YouTube.He wears shirt number 23 in honour of the Australian great and is Japan's leading wicket-taker across pathway and international competitions.Charlie Hara-Hinze, who was part of Japan's U19 Cricket World Cup team that beat Tanzania, has also been included.Spinner Benjamin Ito-Davis is back after his East-Asia Pacific T20 World Cup 2028 Sub-Regional Qualifier campaign was cut short by a hand injury.Japan finished second in the East-Asia Pacific T20 World Cup 2028 Sub-Regional Qualifier.They remain in the race for qualification after finishing level on points with Papua New Guinea. Japan were edged on net run rate despite beating the Barramundis on the final day.The India-Japan match is the first step of “Sport 75”, an initiative that aims to promote human exchanges and cooperation between India and Japan through sport.The initiative comes from an agreement reached during a summit between Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.The agreement also took note of India's ambition to host the Olympic and Paralympic Games in 2036.Japan will play two T20Is against Hong Kong on September 19 and 20, before facing India on September 22.At the Asian Games, Japan will play Afghanistan on September 24 and Nepal on September 26.Japan need to finish in the top two to progress to the quarter-finals.Kendel Kadowaki-Fleming (c), Charlie Hara-Hinze, Benjamin Ito-Davis, Alester Kadowaki-Fleming, Kohei Kubota, Jake Kusuda-Nairn, Wataru Miyauchi (wk), Reo Sakurano-Thomas, Alex Shirai-Patmore (wk), Shoma Sugaya-Slater, Declan Suzuki-McComb, Tsuyoshi Takada, Ibrahim Takahashi, Makoto Taniyama, Lachlan Yamamoto-Lake.
Article Summary: India are the ICC Men's T20 World Cup champions and the No. 1 ranked side. Match will be Japan's first step in their preparation for the Asian Games in Nagoya, which begin two days later. Match is the first step of ‘Sport 75’, an initiative that aims to promote human exchanges and cooperation between India and Japan through sport.

Article Title: "I cried on the court": Coco Gauff opens up about the overwhelming pressure she faces ahead of 2026 US Open quarterfinal

Coco Gauff weighs in on her inspiration and Iva Jovic after her win in Round 4 of the 2026 US Open

Coco Gauff, the 22 year old tennis legend, has been busy in the 2026 US Open as she has advanced to the quarterfinals while being seeded No. 4 in the tournament. As Coco Gauff prepares to go against reigning French Open champion and No. 5 seed Mirra Andreev, her comments on handling pressure have resurfaced.In an interview, the tennis legend Coco Gauff weighed in on her experience in the 2025 US as she said, “I cried on the court, everybody saw that. So yeah, that was the last time I cried. I think for me it just felt like so much pressure in that moment.”The World number 4 champion added, “But I’m kind of happy that I did it, because I felt like people got to see the vulnerability of being an athlete. And also because I created this agenda that I am calm, cool, and collected.”Coco Gauff continued, “And I don’t like when people say that, because it’s not true. So I got to show a little bit of that. But I would not want to feel like that again.”Over the last few years, Coco Gauff has been a force to be reckoned with on the court. The 22 year old star has made a name for herself and has often spoken about how both her parents have sacrificed their own careers to support her.For the unversed, Coco Gauff’s father became her primary tennis coach and gave up on his career in tennis to be by his daughter’s side.Both her parents are also often spotted attending all her matches and cheering her on as Coco Gauff has quickly turned into one of the most promising athletes in the world in the recent few years.A few hours ago, as Coco Gauff beat 18 year old American rising star Iva Jovic (6-1, 6-4) in an 80-minute showcase, she opened up about her win as she said, "Incredible player and incredible talent…”The 22 year old tennis star added, "Give it up for Iva … There was one game when I felt like I was running a marathon. First time I was out of breath on court in a long time."In an interview, Coco Gauff has also spoken about her inspiration as she said, “The WTA player that I admire the most is definitely Serena Williams. Why? I mean, she’s iconic. Everything to her on court fashion and how fierce a competitor she is, and just the representation that she presented for me. She’s an inspiration for me.” she said.

NEW DELHI: A toss before an India vs Pakistan match is always special. But one toss from 1984 has remained memorable for a very different reason.On April 13, 1984, India and Pakistan met at the Sharjah Cricket Stadium in the United Arab Emirates during the inaugural Asia Cup.India captain Sunil Gavaskar and Pakistan captain Zaheer Abbas were at the centre of a light-hearted moment before the match. As the toss took place, Gavaskar jokingly put his foot over the coin, creating a candid moment between the two captains.The match was part of the first-ever Asia Cup, which featured only three teams - India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.India won the toss and decided to bat first and scored 188/4 in 46 overs. Surinder Khanna was India's top scorer with 56 off 72 balls. Sandeep Patil added 43 off 50 balls. Gavaskar stayed unbeaten on 36 off 55 balls. Ghulam Parkar scored 22, while Dilip Vengsarkar made 14.Pakistan's bowlers picked up four wickets, with Shahid Mahboob, Mudassar Nazar and Sarfraz Nawaz among those to take wickets.Pakistan's chase never gathered momentum. They were bowled out for 134 in 39.4 overs.Mohsin Khan top-scored with 35, while Zaheer Abbas made 27.Qasim Umar scored 16 and Saleem Malik made 15, but Pakistan lost wickets regularly.India's bowlers played a major role in the collapse.Roger Binny and Ravi Shastri took three wickets each. Binny finished with 3/33, while Shastri returned figures of 3/40.Pakistan were eventually dismissed for 134, handing India a big victory.India went on to win the first Asia Cup title. The 1984 tournament had just three teams - India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.India have since become the most successful team in Asia Cup history based on the title record provided. India have won the tournament record nine times - 1984, 1988, 1990-91, 1995, 2010, 2016, 2018, 2023 and 2025.Sri Lanka have won the Asia Cup six times, while Pakistan have two titles.Bangladesh have finished runners-up four times, while Afghanistan's best result is a Super Four appearance.
Article Summary: India and Pakistan met at the Sharjah Cricket Stadium in the United Arab Emirates during the inaugural Asia Cup. Sunil Gavaskar and Zaheer Abbas were at the centre of a light-hearted moment before the match. The match was part of the first-ever Asia Cup, which featured only three teams - India, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.

Article Title: Ben Shelton stuns defending champion Carlos Alcaraz to reach US Open semifinals
Article Text:

USA's Ben Shelton produced a stunning performance to beat defending champion Carlos Alcaraz and reach the US Open semifinals at Arthur Ashe Stadium on Wednesday.Shelton defeated World No. 2 Alcaraz in a five-set thriller, winning 6-7, 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, 7-6 to book his place in the last four. The match lasted 4 hours and 28 minutes and ended Alcaraz's 18-match winning streak in Grand Slam tournaments.Shelton will now face fellow American Frances Tiafoe in the semifinals.Tiafoe reached his third US Open semifinal after beating Alex Michelsen 5-7, 3-6, 7-5, 6-3, 7-6 (10-6) on Tuesday.The result guarantees an American player will feature in Sunday's final as the United States continues its wait for a men's major champion since Andy Roddick won the US Open in 2003.Thousands of fans stayed inside Arthur Ashe Stadium until the early hours to watch the match.Shelton received strong support from the home crowd, with fans chanting his name and shouting “USA! USA!” despite Alcaraz's popularity.“It’s incredible," Shelton said. “I always say that this is the greatest sports city in the world, I say that this is the greatest stadium in the world. I’m just hoping that my best friend and my sister over there don’t have to be at work at 6 a.m.in three hours.”Alcaraz won the opening set in a tiebreak, but Shelton quickly changed the momentum.The American won nine games in a row, starting early in the second set and continuing until he moved 3-0 ahead in the third.Alcaraz then fought back and won the fourth set 6-1 to force a deciding set.Alcaraz was playing his first tournament since April after returning from a right wrist injury.The defending champion continued fighting despite vomiting before the start of the final set.The fifth set eventually went to another tiebreak.Alcaraz moved ahead 5-3 after winning four straight points, but Shelton responded with his powerful serving and took advantage of some mistakes from his opponent.Shelton eventually sealed the win with a 146 mph serve that Alcaraz could not return.The victory took Shelton into his third Grand Slam semifinal.He had previously reached the last four at the 2023 US Open and 2025 Australian Open.Alcaraz, meanwhile, is now 15-2 in five-set matches.He had won his seventh Grand Slam title at the Australian Open earlier this year before his injury.
Article Summary: Ben Shelton beats defending champion Carlos Alcaraz in five-set thriller. Shelton will now face fellow American Frances Tiafoe in the semifinals. The result guarantees an American player will feature in Sunday's final. The United States continues its wait for a men's major champion since Andy Roddick in 2003.

KOLKATA: East Zone skipper Ishan Kishan ’s monumental 270 off 334 balls in the Duleep Trophy final has strengthened his case for a return to the Indian Test side, with the Jharkhand wicketkeeper-batter now emerging as a genuine all-format option after an impressive run in international as well as domestic cricket.The innings against South Zone in Chennai was more than just a big score. Coming after a season in which Ishan has consistently delivered in both white-ball and red-ball cricket, it offered a strong indication that he has developed the temperament and game to succeed in the longest format.Former India wicketkeeper Saba Karim believes Ishan’s recent progress reflects a greater maturity in his approach to the game.“The work Ishan has put in at the domestic level over the last season reflects his growing maturity and his desire to be a part of Indian cricket across all three formats. It is good to see him understand his game better and keep improving. The hard work and introspection he has invested in his cricket are now showing in his performances,” Karim told TOI on Tuesday.The conditions made the 270 even more significant. Ishan spent more than nine hours over two days at the crease in Chennai’s heat and humidity, against a strong South Zone attack, to produce one of the most emphatic red-ball statements of his career.“To score 270 in a Duleep Trophy final against a strong South Zone side speaks volumes about his development as a red-ball cricketer. Doing it in Chennai, where the conditions are extremely hot and humid, makes the effort even more special. It was a remarkable innings and I am delighted for him,” Karim said.Former India batter Saurabh Tiwary , Ishan’s senior teammate for Jharkhand, believes the Duleep Trophy performance is a continuation of a broader resurgence rather than an isolated effort. Ishan has also been among the runs in the 2025-26 Ranji Trophy, his highest of the season being 173 from 247 deliveries against Tamil Nadu, in tough batting conditions in Coimbatore.“He has been doing well for some time now, and I can say he is having a golden touch,” Tiwary said. “What’s important is that he has performed not only in white-ball cricket but also in red-ball cricket.”That consistency has now put the Test door firmly within reach.“There is tremendous competition in the Indian team, and it’s never easy to secure a place, but he is certainly knocking on the door,” Tiwary said.Karim feels Ishan’s value to India goes beyond his wicketkeeping credentials, particularly given his ability to contribute in different roles.“Now, with the runs he has scored in red-ball cricket, the Indian team will certainly view him as a strong option in the Test format as well. If your batting is good enough, you can always earn a place as a specialist batter, even if you are primarily known as a wicketkeeper,” he said.The transformation has come through a return to the domestic grind following a season without a BCCI central contract.“One of the most important aspects of a cricketer’s career is responding to setbacks. If you are out of the team, you have to go back to domestic cricket, work hard and become the best performer you can be. Ishan has followed that path,” Karim said.

Kylie Kelce has never been shy about discussing the messy, funny and deeply personal parts of motherhood. On her “Not Gonna Lie” podcast, the mother of four recently turned to a subject many new parents may find awkward to discuss openly: intimacy after childbirth. Her comments mixed humor with a blunt reminder that recovery does not end when a baby arrives.During the March 26, 2026 episode of her podcast, Kylie Kelce spoke about what returning to s*x can feel like after giving birth. Her youngest daughter, Finn, was 11 months old at the time, giving the conversation a personal connection rather than making it a distant discussion about postpartum recovery.Kylie noted that people generally need to wait six to eight weeks before having s*x after childbirth, stressing that healing comes first.“You’re not even allowed to have s*x for six to eight weeks. She’s not ready cause she’s not healed,” Kelce said, while making clear that her comments were based on her experiences with vaginal births.She then delivered the kind of unfiltered observation that has become part of her podcast style.“I’ve had varying experiences, it’s different for every kid. It’s not all fun and games the first couple times, if you catch my drift.We can’t be out here like, ‘Oh that was great,’” she jokingly added. “A human just exited that door.”The joke landed because it captured something often left out of polished conversations about new motherhood. Childbirth can change the body in major ways, and physical recovery does not always follow a neat timetable.Kelce's willingness to say that out loud is part of what makes her discussions resonate. She does not present postpartum life as a smooth transition back to normal. Instead, she talks about the awkwardness, exhaustion and unexpected moments that come with raising children.Her comments also come with an important caveat. Postpartum recovery varies from person to person, and medical guidance should come from a qualified healthcare professional who understands an individual's circumstances.The conversation eventually moved beyond postpartum intimacy and into the bigger question of whether Kylie and Jason Kelce are finished expanding their family.For now, Kylie said that four children feels right. She is raising daughters Wyatt, Elliotte, Bennett and Finn with Jason, but she stopped short of making a permanent declaration about having another baby.“I will say Finny is still just cuddly enough that I do not have an urge for a baby right now," Kelce said. “I like to leave it open-ended, because I don’t want the universe to hear me or my uterus.”That playful uncertainty says plenty about her approach to motherhood. She can be content with where her family is while still leaving room for life to surprise her.And then there is Jason.When Kylie explained why people should not wonder too hard about the couple having four children, she turned the spotlight toward her husband’s post-NFL career.“Let me tell you something,” she quipped. “Don’t ever ask yourself why we have four kids. That’s self-explanatory. Turn on ESPN on Monday night.”Jason Kelce, who retired from the NFL and moved into broadcasting, has become a familiar presence on ESPN. Kylie’s joke offered a glimpse into the couple’s playful relationship while also giving listeners another example of the humor that runs through their family life.At its heart, Kylie Kelce’s conversation was not simply about sex after childbirth. It was about honesty. Motherhood can be beautiful and exhausting, intimate and uncomfortable, all at once. By talking about those contradictions without pretending they are glamorous, Kelce continues to make space for conversations that many parents experience but rarely discuss so openly.

How the trade could impact the New Orleans Pelicans

Jordan Hawkins is heading to Memphis to join Cameron Boozer. The 24-year-old guard was dealt from New Orleans to the Grizzlies on Tuesday in a trade first reported by ESPN's Shams Charania, with forward Micah Peavy, a future second-round pick and a second-round pick swap also headed to Memphis. In return, the Pelicans land AJ Johnson and veteran forward Taj Gibson.The deal has roots in late July, when whispers first emerged that New Orleans was exploring trade frameworks to move Hawkins and create financial breathing room. Memphis, which has spent the past year hoarding draft capital and young talent, turned out to be the perfect landing spot.New Orleans had been shopping $20.6 million former UConn star Jordan Hawkins for weeks, according to Marc Stein and Jake Fischer of The Stein Line, who reported on July 22 that the Pelicans were working through trade frameworks to move him. Michael Scotto of HoopsHype added on July 31 that Johnson had entered those discussions as well. The pieces finally came together Tuesday.For New Orleans, the trade clears space to get Bennedict Mathurin's new contract on the books, a priority that made moving Hawkins almost inevitable. He still had one year and roughly $7 million left on his rookie deal, a manageable number that made him easy to move without much resistance.Memphis, meanwhile, keeps building its war chest. The Grizzlies now hold ten tradable second-round picks and twelve first-round picks across the next seven drafts, nine of which they can deal. Giving up AJ Johnson and Taj Gibson was a small price for a team this deep in assets.Hawkins lands in Memphis carrying more upside than his recent numbers suggest. The Pelicans picked him 14th overall in the 2023 draft, just three months after he helped UConn win a national championship. His rookie season showed flashes of that promise, averaging 7.8 points and shooting 36.6 percent from three across 67 games. His signature moment came against Dallas in January 2024, when he dropped a career-high 34 points in a Pelicans win.His role shrank after that. Last season he played just 51 games, started only once, and averaged 5.1 points in limited minutes. Even so, a career 37.4 percent shooter from the field has value, and Memphis is betting it can unlock the version of Hawkins that torched the NCAA Tournament at 50 percent from deep. If that shooter shows up, the Grizzlies just found themselves a bargain.For New Orleans, this trade is less about what they got and more about what it lets them do next. Offloading Hawkins' salary gives the front office room to lock in Bennedict Mathurin, a move that has been the underlying goal of these talks since July.AJ Johnson gives the Pelicans a young guard already familiar to their front office from earlier trade conversations, while Taj Gibson brings a steady, experienced presence to a locker room that could use one. Giving up a future second-round pick and a swap is a fair cost for the financial flexibility New Orleans gains in return.

Inside Dillon Jones' remarkable run to two championships

Dillon Jones is bringing his rings to Philadelphia. The 76ers signed the 24-year-old forward to an Exhibit 10 contract on Tuesday, ESPN's Dave McMenamin first reported, giving Jones a shot to win a training camp roster spot. Jones spent last season with the Knicks after winning a title with Oklahoma City the year before, making him one of the more unusual free-agent additions in the league this offseason.Philadelphia already added Jaylen Brown and LeBron James this summer, and Jones now joins a growing list of new faces chasing a championship the Sixers have not lifted in decades. He also reunites with Ariel Hukporti, his former Knicks teammate, giving Philadelphia two players who know exactly what it feels like to hoist a trophy.The Sixers made the news official on Tuesday, announcing Dillon Jones' signing in a press release after ESPN's Dave McMenamin broke the news first. "Back-to-back champ Dillon Jones signed with the 76ers to an Exhibit 10 contract," McMenamin wrote, adding that Jones would join Philadelphia's training camp later this month.An Exhibit 10 deal carries no guarantees. It simply gives Philadelphia a low-risk window to evaluate Jones before deciding whether to convert him to a two-way contract or send him to the Delaware Blue Coats.For a player who has bounced through three organizations in two years, it is a familiar kind of audition.Jones gives Philadelphia size and versatility at forward, standing 6-foot-5 and 235 pounds with the strength to guard multiple positions. His NBA numbers do not jump off the page. Across 61 combined games with Oklahoma City and New York, he has averaged just 2.4 points, 2.1 rebounds and 1.0 assist in under ten minutes a night.His G League work tells a different story. Jones averaged 15.2 points, 6.1 assists and 5.6 rebounds in 18 games for the Westchester Knicks last season, shooting close to 38 percent from three after making just 27.5 percent the year before. This kind of jump is exactly what earned him a senior-year MVP award in the Big Sky Conference, where he averaged 20.8 points, 10.1 rebounds and 5.2 assists at Weber State.If that shooting holds up, Philadelphia may have found a legitimate developmental piece buried inside a camp contract.Jones barely played in either title run, appearing in just seven games and 39 minutes for the Knicks and none of them in the playoffs. Coach Mike Brown still leaned on him during the postseason. "I spoke to Dillon often during this playoff run," Brown said on The Roommates Show, explaining that Jones had just gone through a similar run with Oklahoma City.
Article Summary: The Philadelphia 76ers signed Dillon Jones to an Exhibit 10 contract on Tuesday. The 24-year-old forward spent last season with the New York Knicks after winning a title with Oklahoma City the year before. Jones is 6-foot-5 and 235 pounds with strength to guard multiple positions.

NEW DELHI: Olympic medallist Manu Bhaker suffered another personal setback on Tuesday as her 84-year-old grandmother, Daya Kaur, passed away at a private hospital in Rohtak.Daya Kaur had been admitted to the hospital after experiencing chest pain and was also dealing with age-related health complications. Other family members were also away, while her aunt was present at the hospital.Daya Kaur had followed Manu's journey closely, including her historic performance at the Paris Olympics, where Manu became the first Indian athlete since independence to win two medals at a single edition of the Games. She had watched her granddaughter's events from her village and celebrated her success with immense pride.For Manu, the loss is deeply personal. Family members recall the special bond between the two, with Daya Kaur often pampering her granddaughter and feeding her traditional homemade choorma.Manu's shooting commitments are now temporarily on hold as she returns home to be with her family. The Indian shooting team is scheduled to leave on Sept 15.Daya Kaur's last rites will be performed at her native village on Wednesday.

Article Title: Delhi building collapse: Stuck under rubble, student sent live location to friends
Article Text:
Neeraj Bawa and Nitish Chib were sitting together Sunday afternoon when their PG collapsed





NEW DELHI: It had been a hectic few weeks for 19-year-old Neeraj Bawa, who had been campaigning for the upcoming Dusu election and camping with NSUI candidate Vir Chitrath for the past 20 days.On Sunday, as rain forced them to shelve all plans, Neeraj finally returned to Satya Niketan’s Hostel Daze PG. He had just entered his room when suddenly, the walls around him came crashing down.Stuck under a mountain of rubble, he called his friends with a desperate plea: “Bhaiya, please save me. I’ll die here.”A few minutes later, their phone rang again. Neeraj had sent his live location, hoping his friends would come and pull him out soon. Vishnu, one of the boys who reached the site, recounted the frantic search for their friend.“We started to clear debris at the spot where the map located him when, surprisingly, a phone was thrown from a small opening in the rubble.” The lock screen confirmed it was Neeraj’s phone.“Then people started screaming that the adjacent building was also about to collapse, and we ran for our lives. Police didn’t let us go inside again, even though we pleaded that our friend was stuck there,” he said.Neeraj was rescued three hours later, when an NDRF response team pulled him out from the same spot where he had been located by his friends.Back at his home in Jammu’s Kathua, Neeraj’s family had been constantly calling him after hearing that a building had collapsed in Satya Niketan.“Neeraj’s sister, who was watching live coverage of the collapse on TV, recognised the rakhi on his hand as he was taken out. That was when we realised it was his PG that had fallen, and that he was injured,” said Ashok Kumar, a relative.After being pulled out, Neeraj was operated upon at AIIMS Trauma Centre Sunday. On Tuesday, Neeraj underwent a second surgery and remains in a critical condition, according to his family.The teenager had come to Delhi two years ago to pursue a commerce degree from Motilal Nehru College in DU’s South Campus. There he met Nishant Chib, who was also from Jammu, and they became good friends.Neeraj and Nishant moved into different rooms in Hostel Daze PG, but “they would sit together all day in each other’s rooms. It was as if they were roommates,” said Divvy, a mutual friend of theirs.The boys were sitting together Sunday afternoon when their PG collapsed. Nishant told his mother, Seema, that they were separated only by a block of concrete and he could hear Neeraj’s urgent cry for help.Nishant was rescued a few minutes before Neeraj with a head injury. He is currently receiving treatment at AIIMS and is in a stable condition.Locals said the PG, which crumbled like a stack of cards, was one of the most expensive ones in Satya Niketan. According to their friends, Neeraj and Nishant were paying around Rs 15,000 each for a bed in the building.While seven people died in the collapse, five others were injured, two of whom are critical.
Article Summary: Neeraj Bawa and Nitish Chib were sitting together Sunday afternoon when their PG collapsed. Neeraj was rescued three hours later, when an NDRF response team pulled him out from the same spot where he had been located by his friends. Nishant was rescued a few minutes later with a head injury.

Article Title: Delhi building collapse: Already dealt a bad hand, 2 workers meet untimely end
Article Text:
Paramlal Kori had worked at the Satya Niketan PG facility for only four days when the disaster unfolded Sunday afternoon





NEW DELHI: Paramlal Kori, 30,was the sole breadwinner of his family, living in a rented room in Humayunpur, Safdarjung Enclave, with his wife Vandana and their five-year-old son. He had recently enrolled his son in Class I at a govt school, hoping to secure a better future for him.Paramlal had worked at the Satya Niketan PG facility for only four days when the disaster unfolded Sunday afternoon.That morning, he left for work around 8.30am as usual, carrying lunch packed by Vandana. When he failed to return home that night, a frantic Vandana repeatedly called his phone, only to find it switched off.The following morning, she rushed to the collapse site, clutching a photograph of her husband and pleading for information.By afternoon, her worst fears were confirmed when officials informed the family that Paramlal had died in the collapse, leaving his wife and young son without any source of income.“My husband died under the rubble… Our future looks bleak now. I hope govt helps us with compensation,” Vandana said, adding, “I will work now to raise my son.”A native of Madhya Pradesh, Paramlal moved to Delhi with his family in search of work. He had been living in the city for nearly 20 years, finding odd jobs as a welder. His brother Mukesh said Paramlal earned about Rs 1,200 a day.On Tuesday, Paramlal’s body was taken to his native village in Madhya Pradesh, where his last rites were performed.The tragedy also claimed the life of 56-year-old Surender Singh, who lived with his wife, son and daughter in Arjan Nagar.Tejpal, who worked with him, said Surender was a “calm and quiet man” who had been working as a welder for several years. “He never had a fight with anyone. He kept to himself and was focused on his work,” Tejpal said.After learning about the collapse, Tejpal went to the site with Paramlal’s wife Vandana to search for the two men. They were later told that the injured had been taken to a hospital. The two then rushed there, only to receive the devastating news about their deaths.Mukesh said he had also earlier worked under Surender, who used to take up contracts. Surender’s son was also an earning member of the family and worked elsewhere.Amid the overwhelming grief, the family of DU student Abhishek, who also died in the collapse, found a way to give others a chance at life by donating his eyes.Speaking to media, his father urged govt to take strict action and ensure such a tragedy is not repeated. “Those responsible should be held accountable so that no other family has to suffer a similar loss,” he said.
Article Summary: Paramlal Kori, 30, was the sole breadwinner of his family, living in a rented room in Humayunpur, Safdarjung Enclave. He had recently enrolled his son in Class I at a govt school, hoping to secure a better future for him. Paramlal had worked at the Satya Niketan PG facility for only four days when the disaster unfolded Sunday afternoon.

Article Title: “Three-against-one situation”: El Rubius opens up on being “targeted” in MrBeast’s viral $1M challenge
Article Text:
El Rubius reacted honestly after his elimination from MrBeast’s $1 million challenge, calling it “unfair” and claiming he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings. His response felt real and balanced, especially after MrBeast’s team later sent him a cake, softening the moment.

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit

El Rubius did not just walk away from MrBeast’s $1 million streamer challenge. He opened up. Soon after his elimination, the Spanish creator shared a raw reaction with fans, giving them a closer look at what the experience felt like from inside the game. It was not polished or carefully framed. It felt real, and that is exactly why it caught attention so quickly.The clip and his response have since fueled conversations across the streaming space. Some viewers believe intense competitions like this naturally lead to uneven situations. Others feel Rubius may have had a point about being singled out. Either way, his words have added a human layer to a challenge that many only saw as entertainment.Speaking through an Instagram Story, Rubius did not hide his frustration, but he also made sure to thank his supporters. He said, "Guys, I just got knocked out of the game. It was a bit of an unfair elimination, but hey, at least I managed to walk away with $50,000 for you all, which I’ve already distributed. It went to the mods, the subs, and the non-subs alike."He further added, "I’m happy, of course, though admittedly, it was incredibly tough.I wasn't really a fan of the challenge itself, either. But then again... it was basically a three-against-one situation the entire time. I mean, they were targeting me specifically the whole way through. I kept trying to go after RaKai, but, well, he actually just got eliminated in the end. So, at least justice was served for Abraham. Abraham, if you’re watching this, we were all rooting for you, and standing right there with you."His message carried mixed emotions. There was disappointment, yes, but also pride in how he handled things. Giving away his $50,000 winnings to his community stood out as a gesture that meant more than the result itself.He continued with another honest note, saying, "And in the end, karma finally caught up with that little punk. Sorry, I’m being a bit toxic right now, but let's just hope the MrBeast team doesn't see this! Guys, thank you all so much. Seriously, thank you for all the support and for just being there."He added, "Every time I asked for something in the chat or whatever it was, you guys were right there. You’re incredible. I’m a little disappointed in myself, personally, mostly for not performing better, but hey, I gave it my all, and we still walked away with $50,000, so we’ve got to look on the bright side. All right, guys, big hugs to all my brothers out there!"Interestingly, the story did not end with frustration. Later that day, Rubius revealed that MrBeast’s team had sent him a cake after his exit. It was a small gesture, but it shifted the mood. It showed that even in a high-pressure challenge, there is still room for respect.In the end, Rubius’ reaction felt honest and grounded. That is what stayed with people.
Article Summary: El Rubius was eliminated from MrBeast's $1 million streamer challenge. He called it "unfair" and said he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings.

The comprehensive win also meant RCB have registered four consecutive triumphs over CSK for the first time in the IPL’s history.

Article Title: "Trans women are.....": Clavicular’s viral moment with trans women sparks fresh conversation on internet culture
Article Text:
A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Instead of conflict, the exchange highlights shared influence and mutual awareness. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration rather than ownership.

Clavicular and trans women share a surprising realization about online trends

The video of Clavicular, a short-video producer, is going around the Internet, yet not the reason why. There is no yelling or over-the-top drama. It is a mere, everyday talk that seems almost novel nowadays, in the age of internet, which is overflowing with content. The scene is easy-going, the tone of the narrative is straightforward, and the characters appear more concerned with conversation than combat.The message that is being addressed is the flow of the conversation. It discusses internet culture, the way people communicate with one another and the place of trends. Rather than bringing out a debate, the encounter towards curiosity. It quietly brings attention to something that a lot of people who use the internet notice but don't often say out loud. People in different communities often have a bigger impact on each other than they think.The conversation begins with a confident and lighthearted comment from one of the trans women present. She says, "You know that trans women are like the OG lip masters, right? We are very talented in the program. Like, I do the peptides, I'm on Zeta." Her tone carries a mix of pride and humor, setting a relaxed vibe at the table.Clavicular responds in a way that keeps the mood steady but adds a different angle.He says, "That is funny because you guys were using a lot of the words in like the South Korean subreddits in like 2014." It’s not confrontational. If anything, it feels like an observation. He points to how certain words and ideas may have traveled across different online spaces over time.Another voice joins in and brings the moment full circle. "Guys, we're like the OGs. I saw a couple of posts about that. We're like copying each other." That line hits in a simple but honest way. It reflects something familiar. Online culture is rarely created in isolation. It grows through sharing, borrowing, and sometimes even unknowingly repeating.That's what makes the clip so powerful. It doesn't want to make a point or win an argument. It only shows a group of people talking, listening, and figuring something out together.This moment feels different in a space where viral content often leads to fights. It reminds people that conversations can be calm, thoughtful, and still important. And sometimes, that honest silence is what makes it work.

Article Title: Who was Rakesh Mehta? Delhi ex-CS who readied city for 2010 Games found dead
Article Text:
Former Delhi chief secretary Rakesh Mehta was found dead in his Noida flat.

Rakesh Mehta's role in Delhi's public transport

Education and personal life





NOIDA: Former Delhi chief secretary and municipal commissioner Rakesh Mehta , 74, was found dead at his rented flat in Sector 82 on Sunday afternoon.Police recovered a one-page note in which the retired bureaucrat referred to his illnesses and stated that no one was responsible for his death.Mehta, a 1975-batch AGMUT-cadre IAS officer, took charge as Delhi chief secretary in December 2007 during the tenure of then chief minister Sheila Dikshit. He remained in the post until 2010, with his tenure coinciding with preparations for the 2010 Commonwealth Games, one of the biggest administrative challenges faced by the capital.Before becoming chief secretary, Mehta held several key positions in the Delhi administration. He served as MCD commissioner, chairman and managing director of the Delhi Transport Corporation (DTC), and secretary (power). He was known for his focus on urban governance and public transport.During his tenure at DTC, Mehta oversaw the transition away from the accident-prone Blue Line buses and the introduction of low-floor buses, which later became a familiar feature of Delhi's roads.As chief secretary, Mehta was known as a media-savvy bureaucrat who pushed new projects and administrative reforms. After taking charge, he unveiled a 10-point agenda and advocated greater transparency in civic administration.He also backed changes to building bylaws and promoted the use of technology to make government services more accessible to citizens.Mehta studied at St Stephen's College, Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) and the London School of Economics.He had been living alone at Central Vihar-2 in Noida for around five years. His wife, also a retired Delhi-cadre IAS officer, and their son live in Dehradun, while their married daughter is based in London. Family members visited him in Noida from time to time.According to police, Mehta's wife last spoke to him on Saturday night. When repeated calls went unanswered on Sunday afternoon, family members alerted the society's security staff. Two guards went to his flat and found him dead in one of the rooms. A police team and a relative living nearby arrived soon afterwards.A forensic team examined the flat and collected evidence before the body was sent for an autopsy. Till late Tuesday night, the family had not lodged any complaint, though police said an inquiry had been initiated into the circumstances surrounding the death.Family members said Mehta had been suffering from hypertension, diabetes and other health problems, including tremors in his right hand and leg.Mehta's final rites were held in Delhi on Monday.
Article Summary: Rakesh Mehta, 74, was found dead at his rented flat in Noida on Sunday. Police recovered a one-page note in which the retired bureaucrat referred to his illnesses and stated that no one was responsible for his death. He had been suffering from hypertension, diabetes and other health problems.
