There the team was allegedly abused, assaulted and pushed, and their official work was obstructed. In the second incident, four unidentified assailants on two motorcycles allegedly attacked Right to Information activist Ashok Khade with wooden sticks.

Article Title: Khalapur temple theft: Video shows masked man stealing silver Padukas; 2 arrested in Pune
Article Text:
he accused stole silver Charan Paduka from Shree Swami Samarth temple on September 2





NAVI MUMBAI: The Khalapur police probing the theft case wherein a masked man had decamped with a pair of silver toe-knob sandals (Charan Paduka) representing divine footprints offered at Shree Swami Samarth temple in Khalapur city on September 2, have arrested the acccused thief and his aide by tracking them to Pune on Monday.Pradeep Rayannavar, senior inspector of Khalapur informed that, the arrested accused are Mahendrasingh Rathod, 45, who hails from Rajasthan and Ravi Soni, 32, who hails from UP and is a history-sheeter as a theft case is registered against him in Pune.Both were presently residing in Chikhali, Pune district.On September 2, the temple trustee Deepak Bodarde, 68, lodged a complaint of theft of silver Padukas from the temple.When the CCTV footage of the temple premises was checked, it was seen that a masked man wearing a hat and attired in white Kurta-Payjama entering the temple around 7.30am.He goes to the first floor of the temple where the silver Padukas were kept in front of the idol of Shree Swami Samarth.By pretending to offer prayers, he picked up the Padukas and hid them inside his Kurta and exited the temple.Inspector Rayannavar said," The theft was committed when the temple priest had gone to his room near the temple.Upon checking the CCTV footage of the roads near the temple, it was seen that two masked men on a bike were loitering near the temple and conducted a reece before committing the theft.""Considering the religious sentiments of the devotees, Raigad SP forms a special police team to detect the case at the earliest. Subsequently, the CCTV footage along the escape route of the thieves were scanned. The bike used in the crime did not have a registration number plate," Rayannavar added.He further said, "However, using technical expertise, intelligence inputs and footages of CCTV camera along the highways, the thieves on bike were tracked and apprehended from Chikhali in Pune district. We have seized from them the stolen Padukas and the bike used in the crime. On Monday, the acccused were produced before the Khalapur JMFC court that remanded them to police custody till Friday."
Article Summary: A pair of silver toe-knob sandals (Charan Paduka) representing divine footprints offered at Shree Swami Samarth temple in Khalapur city were stolen on September 2. The accused thief and his aide were arrested by tracking them to Pune on Monday.

Article Title: Cop dies by suicide at Navi Mumbai lodge, names ex-DCP, ACP and head clerk in note alleging harassment
Article Text:
The deceased identified as Pandurang Nimba Patil, a resident of Airoli.





NAVI MUMBAI: A 55-year-old Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) with the Navi Mumbai Police allegedly died by suicide at a lodge in Airoli on Saturday evening.The deceased, identified as Pandurang Nimba Patil, a resident of Airoli, had recorded a video before taking the drastic step and posted it on social media.In the video, he alleged that he was compelled to end his life due to harassment by a former DCP, an ACP, and a head clerk.ASI Patil also left behind a nine-page suicide note accusing former DCP (Headquarters) Sanjay Patil, ACP Girish Thakare, and administrative head clerk Jayu Ahire of driving him to take the extreme step by allegedly harassing him while assigning official duties.ACP (Rabale Division) Rahul Dhas said, "ASI Patil had checked into Sachi Lodging and Boarding on Saturday at 4.40 pm. Around 7.30 pm, when the housekeeping staff went to his room, he did not respond, and the door was locked from inside. The lodge manager opened the door with a master key and found ASI Patil hanging from a ceiling fan hook. The lodge manager informed the Rabale MIDC police. ASI Patil was rushed to NMMC Hospital in Vashi, where he was declared brought dead. Prima facie, an accidental death case will be registered at the Rabale MIDC police station."
Article Summary: Pandurang Nimba Patil, a 55-year-old Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) with the Navi Mumbai Police, allegedly died by suicide at a lodge in Airoli on Saturday evening. He recorded a video before taking the drastic step and posted it on social media. In the video, he alleged that he was compelled to end his life due to harassment by a former DCP, an ACP, and a head clerk.

Article Title: 12-year-old girl, young woman rescued from prostitution racket in Navi Mumbai
Article Text:
Cops can be seen walking with 2 women. (AI-generated image used for representational purpose)





NAVI MUMBAI: The Anti-Human Trafficking Unit (AHTU) of Navi Mumbai crime branch rescued a 12-year-old girl and a 26-year-old woman from a prostitution racket being carried out at a lodge in Nerul after conducting a raid by sending a decoy customer on Thursday.The police have arrested two managers of the lodge and a waiter for allegedly supplying women for prostitution to customers by providing them rooms at Kohinoor Palace Lodging and Boarding in Shiravane village, Nerul.Gajanan Kadam, AHTU senior inspector, said the rescued minor girl hails from UP and resided in Shiravane village with her cousins, who had brought her from UP after telling her parents that she would be given a job.The trap was laid after receiving a tip-off about prostitution being carried out at the lodge. A decoy customer was sent to the lodge, where he demanded a woman for sexual favours after booking a room. The accused demanded Rs 4,000 for supplying a woman.After the accused accepted the amount, the decoy customer signalled the police team waiting outside the lodge, following which they raided the premises.Inspector Kadam said, “The arrested accused are the lodge managers identified as Hridaykumar Singh and Deepak Ramrakhiani and the waiter Kuleshwar Kumar Singh.”At Nerul police station, an FIR was registered against the arrested accused by invoking BNS sections for trafficking of persons and joint criminal liability, along with the POCSO Act, which defines punishment for abetment, such as helping, encouraging or plotting any sexual crime against a child, and the Prevention of Immoral Traffic Act.On Friday, the three accused were produced before the Belapur JMFC court, which remanded them to police custody till Sept 9.
Article Summary: The police have arrested two managers of the lodge and a waiter for allegedly supplying women for prostitution to customers. The trap was laid after receiving a tip-off about prostitution being carried out at the lodge. A decoy customer was sent to the lodge, where he demanded a woman for sexual favours.

Article Title: Maharashtra horror: Teen murdered, body dumped near Mini Seashore
Article Text:
A 19-year-old man was found murdered near a public garden in Vashi





NAVI MUMBAI: A 19-year-old boy was murdered and his body was dumped on the pavement near a public garden along Mini Seashore Road in Sector 10A, Vashi, early on Saturday morning. The Vashi police have registered a murder case against unidentified accused.Shashikant Chandekar, senior inspector of Vashi police station, said, "The murder victim was identified as Sujan Kumar Mahato, a resident of Sector 19, Koparkhairane. A passing pedestrian spotted him lying unconscious in a pool of blood on the pavement around 4am. The pedestrian alerted Vashi police station, and our police team reached the spot and took the teenager to NMMC Hospital in Vashi, where he was declared brought dead due to severe blood loss from grievous injuries to his head and wrist after being assaulted with some sharp lethal weapon. The victim Mahato hails from Bihar and resided with his father, who is an auto-rickshaw driver, his mother and two minor siblings. He worked at a roadside Chinese food stall in Koparkhairane and used to drive his father's auto-rickshaw during the night."Inspector Chandekar added, "Mahato had left home on Friday around 9pm, telling his mother that he was going to work at the Chinese food stall and was taking his father's auto-rickshaw to ferry passengers throughout the night.After his body was found early on Saturday morning, his family was informed. His father's auto-rickshaw was not found at the crime scene. Hence, it is suspected that after fatally assaulting Mahato, the assailant took away the auto-rickshaw, which is being traced by scanning CCTV footage along the route from Koparkhairane to Vashi."As there is no CCTV camera surveillance near the crime scene, we are scanning CCTV footage from roads leading to the crime spot where Mahato's body was dumped to zero in on the suspect. Mahato might have been fatally assaulted at the spot, or he might have been assaulted at another location and his body brought in a vehicle and dumped near Mini Seashore. Accordingly, using technical expertise, efforts are being made to detect the murder case. Meanwhile, Mahato's kin and friends are being questioned to get some lead on the unidentified accused."
Article Summary: A 19-year-old man was found murdered near a public garden in Vashi. The Vashi police have registered a murder case against unidentified accused. The victim was identified as Sujan Kumar Mahato, a resident of Sector 19, Koparkhairane.

Article Title: 3 youths treckking to Chanderi fort near Panvel miss way, get stranded; rescued by cops
Article Text:
The rescued youths aged 22-25 years were identified as Om Khilari, Parth Kadve and Rushil Vrindavan.





NAVI MUMBAI: Three youths from Kamothe who went trekking to Chanderi Fort near Panvel lost their way and got stranded before being rescued by the Panvel Taluka Police on Sunday.Gajanan Ghadge, Senior Inspector of Panvel Taluka Police Station, said that the rescued youths, aged between 22 and 25 years, were identified as Om Khilari, Parth Kadve and Rushil Vrindavan. They had started their trek at around 8 am.At around 11 am, the police helpline number 112 received a distress call from one of the trekkers, informing officials that they had lost their way while trekking towards Chanderi Fort."Upon receiving the information, we contacted the caller and asked him to share his live Google location. Accordingly, our police team, along with the Wavanje check-post beat marshal, Ritghar village head Deepak Patil, and the rescue team of NGO Sahyadri Pratishthan, launched a search operation by tracking the youth's mobile location," Ghadge said.The three youths were located within an hour in the hilly terrain and were safely brought down to the foothills.
Article Summary: Three youths from Kamothe who went trekking to Chanderi Fort near Panvel lost their way. They were rescued by the Panvel Taluka Police on Sunday. The youths were located within an hour in the hilly terrain and were safely brought down to the foothills.

Article Title: Pet dog battles leopard at MNS ex-MLA’s brother’s farmhouse in Thane, forces it to flee
Article Text:
A pet dog named Rocky bravely confronted a leopard in Thane's Sakhare village





THANE: In a dramatic encounter caught on camera, a pet dog put up a fierce fight against a leopard that strayed into a farmhouse in Sakhare village in Thane district's Murbad taluka on Monday evening, successfully forcing the big cat to retreat.The incident took place around 7:22pm at a farmhouse owned by Vijay Patil, brother of former Maharashtra Navnirman Sena (MNS) MLA Pramod (Raju) Patil.CCTV footage of the incident, which has gone viral on social media, shows the leopard stealthily entering the farmhouse veranda from the adjoining forested patch and attempting to pounce on the pet canine, named Rocky, from behind.​Alerted by the ambush, Rocky initially scrambled away to gain his footing before turning around to confront the predator head-on.A tense, intense scuffle ensued right on the porch, with the canine refusing to back down. After a prolonged face-off, the exhausted predator gave up and fled into the darkness.Rocky sustained minor injuries in the scuffle but is reported to be safe and out of danger.​The incident has triggered panic among residents in Sakhare and nearby villages, where human-wildlife encounters have been steadily rising due to settlements and farmhouses bordering thick Murbad forest cover.With the big cat now entering residential compounds, alarmed locals have urged the forest department to step up vigil and immediately place cages to capture the leopard.
Article Summary: A pet dog named Rocky bravely confronted a leopard in Thane's Sakhare village. The big cat strayed into a farmhouse in Murbad taluka on Monday evening. Rocky sustained minor injuries in the scuffle but is reported to be safe and out of danger.

Article Title: Another Pawar vs Pawar battle brews: NCP (SP) to field candidates against NCP in sugar mill poll
Article Text:
Deputy CM and NCP chief Sunetra Pawar

Pune:

Veteran politician Sharad Pawar





Someshwar Cooperative Sugar Mill election in Baramati is set for another Pawar-versus-Pawar showdown, as merger talks between the two NCP factions appear to have hit a wall.Sharad Pawar-led NCP (SP) has announced that it will field candidates against NCP, led by deputy CM Sunetra Pawar, in the upcoming election to the influential cooperative sugar mill, whose membership spans Baramati, Purandar and Phaltan.The mill was long associated with former deputy CM Ajit Pawar , and undivided NCP had swept the last elections. Following the split in the party, however, most members have aligned with NCP, now led by Sunetra.Ahead of next month’s polls, Sunetra recently addressed a gathering of members and farmers, with NCP appealing for an unopposed election in view of Ajit Pawar’s sudden demise on Jan 28.Signalling a contest, Sharad Pawar ’s grandnephew and NCP (SP) member Yugendra Pawar on Monday said his party would enter the fray. “Till Ajit Pawar was alive, he managed the affairs of the Someshwar sugar factory efficiently and there was little need for anyone else to intervene.After his demise, members want Sharad Pawar’s guidance. That is why we have decided to contest the election,” Yugendra said.Despite the announcement, efforts for a consensus remain under way. NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar said the election should ideally be unopposed, with both sides working out a formula to elect representatives without a contest.Yugendra also left the door open for negotiations. “If the other side comes forward with a formula, we are willing to discuss it and consider an unopposed election. But for now, we are preparing for the poll,” he said.
Article Summary: Sharad Pawar-led NCP (SP) has announced that it will field candidates against NCP, led by deputy CM Sunetra Pawar. NCP appealed for an unopposed election in view of Ajit Pawar’s sudden demise on Jan 28. Despite the announcement, efforts for a consensus remain under way.

Article Title: Anti-narcotics cell arrests two with MD worth Rs1.5L in Nashik
Article Text:
Nashik

:





The anti-narcotics cell of Nashik city police arrested two youths in Mhasrul area, and seized 56g of mephedrone (MD) worth Rs1.5 lakh. The police also seized a two-wheeler and cell phones, bringing the total value of the seized property to Rs2.14 lakh.The arrested suspects have been identified as Darshan Gorakh Gaikwad (22) and Roshan Dinkar Lokhande (23), both residents of Matori of Nashik taluka.PI Ramdas Shelke of anti-narcotics cell said that on Monday at around 8.30pm, a Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances patrolling team spotted a two-wheeler parked suspiciously near an open ground, close to an auto-rickshaw stand at Ashwamedh Nagar. Upon noticing two youths behaving suspiciously, the team alerted PI Ramdas Shelke.Acting on instructions from DCP (Crime) Kirankumar Chavan and ACP (Crime) Sandip Mitke, a specialised team led by API Vishal Patil, Sachin Chaudhari, and PSI Ranjan Bendale raided the spot. Although the suspects tried to flee, officers surrounded and intercepted them.During the search conducted in the presence of a forensic team, officers recovered 21.5g of MD worth Rs 64,500 from one of Darshan Gaikwad’s pockets and another 35.5g worth Rs1.05 lakh from his other pocket. During interrogation, Gaikwad confessed that he procured 25g of the contraband from a Nashik-based supplier, and brought the remaining 35g from Mumbai.The operation was carried out as per the guidance of CP Sandeep Karnik to curb drug peddling across the city. A case was registered at the Mhasrul police station against both suspects and their accomplices.
Article Summary: The anti-narcotics cell of Nashik city police arrested two youths in Mhasrul area, and seized 56g of mephedrone. The police also seized a two-wheeler and cell phones, bringing the total value of the seized property to Rs2.14 lakh. The arrested suspects have been identified as Darshan Gorakh Gaikwad and Roshan Dinkar Lokhande.

Article Title: Nashik Rural police arrest two in theft case
Article Text:
Nashik:





The Ozar Police in Nashik Rural have arrested two suspects who, while posing as sadhus, duped a local trader in broad daylight and fled with his gold jewellery.Acting on the complaint, the team traced the duo to the banks of the Narmada river in Madhya Pradesh and recovered melted gold blocks worth Rs2.8 lakh.The incident took place on Aug 22 in Ozar. The complainant, a 45-year-old sweets-shop owner, was approached by the two men in the afternoon. They first gained his trust and then took his gold rings valued at around Rs1 lakh before fleeing.As per the complainant, the impostors who arrived at his shop on a motorcycle initially demanded a big donation for a religious feast in Trimbakeshwar. Though the complainant initially told them that he could not pay the donation, one of the accused placed a cone-shaped item on the former’s palm as prasad and after chanting some mantra, pretended to transform it into a rudraksha.One of the suspects, after asking the shopkeeper to stretch out his hands, removed two gold rings from his hand, put them in his mouth and left. Realising that he was cheated, the shopkeeper registered a complaint with Ozar police station.Inpector Mahesh Kulkarni of Ozar police station said the breakthrough came through rigorous technical analysis and meticulous review of footage from over 45 CCTV cameras along the escape route of the suspects. The trail led the team to Khalghat, along Narmada River in Madhya Pradesh, where the officers arrested the duo from a crowded area.The accused have been identified as Jalimnath Kalunath (25) and Bandhannath Madhunath (26), both residents of Kasrawad in MP’s Khargone district.The duo were produced in court and have been remanded in two-day police custody.
Article Summary: The incident took place on Aug 22 in Ozar. The complainant, a 45-year-old sweets-shop owner, was approached by the two men in the afternoon. They first gained his trust and then took his gold rings valued at around Rs1 lakh before fleeing.

Article Title: Nashik markets brim with decor as Ganeshotsav nears
Article Text:
Nashik

:





With Ganesh Chaturthi around the corner, Nashik markets are witnessing a surge in demand for festive decor, with stalls in Shalimar, Raviwar Peth, Main Road, Nashik Road and Pawan Nagar in CIDCO drawing buyers looking for home Ganesh setup supplies.Decorating the deity’s space holds deep cultural significance, with families spending time planning elaborate setups that reflect their devotion. Shops offer decorative materials and ready-made setups ranging from ₹500 to ₹25,000.“We have prefabricated setups, including grand temple replicas, ornate arches, and open-to-the-sky models. There are vibrant colour schemes on offer, supplemented by intricate arrangements of decorative lighting and bright miniature LED lamps that add a shimmering finish to the setups,” said Shashank Kale, a shopkeeper in Pawan Nagar.Ready-made sets are particularly popular among families seeking a convenient yet elaborate look. “We see the highest demand for ready-made temple backdrops and lighting sets right before the festival,” said Ramesh Shinde, a shopkeeper at Raviwar Peth. “It is for the families who want complete, hassle-free setups that can be assembled quickly without compromising on grand aesthetics.”Buyers, too, appreciate the convenience. “The ready-made arches with LED arrangements save us a lot of setup time,” said Sunita Patil, a buyer in the market.“With prices ranging from ₹500 to ₹25,000, it is easy to find something that fits our home space and budget.”At the same time, many devotees continue to prefer making their decorations from scratch using handmade paper, fabric drapes, bamboo frames and floral garlands.“When everyone joins in to prepare and decorate, the festival comes alive through shared thoughts and collective effort. Buying ready-made items simply can’t match that warmth, as it shifts the experience from active involvement to passive effort,” said Amit Deshmukh, a resident buying raw craft supplies.
Article Summary: With Ganesh Chaturthi around the corner, Nashik markets are witnessing a surge in demand for festive decor. ready-made sets are particularly popular among families seeking a convenient yet elaborate look. Many devotees continue to prefer making their decorations from scratch using handmade paper, fabric drapes, bamboo frames and floral garlands.
